checks.label: Each symbol is drawn in its normal or neutral condition: the press opens with both solenoids off, the middle box against the ports, P to T unloading the pump and the ram held near the top
When pressure is applied to the top chamber, the bottom chamber is aligned to drain back to the reservoir: with -Y1 the left box feeds A at the top and lines B at the bottom up to T
With the supply connected to the piston side and the rod side exhausted, the pressure on the piston side advances the rod: -Y3 feeds the piston side, exhausts the rod side and the rod comes out
With -Y1 the ram comes down, stops on the work and all the pump's oil then goes over the relief valve; with -Y2 it goes back up, and at the top the oil goes over the relief valve
Stopped with the ram on the work, the line from A stays under pressure; stopped with the ram above it, the line from B; either way the gauge reads zero
Pressure times volume stays the same: 6 × 300 = 1800, so 9 bar absolute gives 200 cm³ and 12 gives 150 cm³; each step up in pressure squeezes the air smaller
Worked by hand: 1800 ÷ 9 = 200 cm³; the slips are the pressures upside down, 300 × 9 ÷ 6 = 450, and no squeeze at all, 300; the field asks exactly this
Going down, the rod side's oil leaves through the flow control, then the valve, then the tank; going up it passes the check valve, which lets oil only into the rod side

Before an answer nothing gives it away: puzzles open with no switches, rings or pulse; screens 3, 7, 9 and 14 show no flow, screen 5 lights only the path into the piston side, screen 11 only the supply, screen 13 draws no red line, and screen 1 only 300 cm³ at 6 bar
Every demonstration settles within 4.5 s, and every answer's motion within 3 s
